findings.Fix: pick one: either she says it or she doesn't; don't perform the avoidance and then immediately violate it

findings.Quote: He looked like a man reading a river junction - here is the situation, here are the exits, here is what will matter in the next hour.
findings.Note: list-cadence aphorism that explains the character's mind rather than showing it through action
findings.Fix: cut the triad and let one concrete observed behavior stand for it

findings.Quote: he did not stop short of finishing things
findings.Note: vague characterizing tag, tells trait rather than showing it
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a specific instance of him finishing something

findings.Quote: Lyra read the shape of what six months of Vega's work had resolved into, standing at last on the ground the work had been describing the whole time without either sister present to see it - fast, whole, no assembly re
findings.Note: sentence cuts off mid-thought, leaving the beat's climactic emotional payoff (reunion/loss motif with the sister) unresolved and unreadable
findings.Fix: complete the sentence so the beat lands

findings.Quote: He paused. The Singing Spires vibrated in the pause. Everyone felt it.
findings.Note: the environmental detail is used as portentous punctuation rather than doing new work; borders on stock 'ominous silence' beat
findings.Fix: cut or tie the vibration to a specific character reaction instead of a generic 'everyone felt it'

findings.Quote: Ocipheus did not number its people, though. He wanted a code where she had only a name. M-1018883 had a number stamped where a name used to be. She had a name where the Canon wanted a number, and the reach closed on nothing.
findings.Note: overwritten, repetitive restating of the same idea four times in slightly different phrasing; muddles rather than clarifies the point
findings.Fix: cut to one clean sentence: he reached for a code that didn't exist for her, and the citation failed

findings.Quote: Holding the small wet wound over the enormous one below, she understood something she would never prove and never stop seeing: they were the same kind of thing.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound summary statement that tells the reader the thematic point instead of trusting the established imagery to carry it
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the parallel stand on the prior images alone

findings.Quote: Every other Scry she had made in seventeen years was a look taken and given back... She had spent seventeen years treating the Oculus as the same act, only longer
findings.Note: If she treated the Oculus the same as every other Scry, it wasn't 'every other Scry' - the Oculus is being both excluded and included in the seventeen-year pattern
findings.Fix: Clarify: 'Every other Scry... Only the Oculus she had treated as the same act, only longer'

findings.Quote: Not shock crossed his face. Not the look of a man whose plan had been destroyed. He was not that kind of man.
findings.Note: Triple negative construction telling us what emotion isn't present is a weak substitute for showing what is; 'He was not that kind of man' is a flat authorial assertion
findings.Fix: Cut the assertion; describe the actual expression directly

findings.Quote: She knew it the way she knew the weight of a shield about to take a blow.
findings.Note: Abstract simile comparing knowledge of a person's mental state to physical weight-anticipation doesn't hold up literally - a shield's weight is static and known in advance, not an anticipatory sensation
findings.Fix: Replace with a more literal comparison drawn from her actual combat experience with him

findings.Quote: the shell went slack and empty
findings.Note: Stock 'body as empty shell' imagery for dissociation/absence
findings.Fix: Specify a more particular physical marker unique to this character's condition

findings.Quote: I am not the person who authorized its release. I am the person who certified the authorization. Vega had not underlined it. She had not needed to.
findings.Note: The italicized aphorism plus the follow-up commentary is a pseudo-profound flourish explaining its own cleverness — telling the reader how to feel about the line instead of trusting it.
findings.Fix: Cut 'She had not needed to' or the whole trailing beat; let the quoted line stand alone.

findings.Quote: Not with anger. Not with what she would have called respect, and not with its absence either - something between the two, the specific look of a competent practitioner who has just watched someone else handle a mechanism correctly.
findings.Note: Overqualified negation chain (not X, not Y, not absence of Y) circles the emotion rather than landing it — a hedge dressed as precision.
findings.Fix: Compress to one clean description: 'A professional's look — the recognition of a mechanism well handled.'

findings.Quote: He was the kind of man who understood exactly what that meant.
findings.Note: Generic character-summary sentence, a stock 'he was the kind of man who' construction that tells rather than dramatizes.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the following list of assets demonstrate his understanding.

findings.Quote: Not quite a joke. The plain statement of a man who had spent his working life at the edge of the membrane's secrets with a handmade tool, and had arrived at a place where the tool was unnecessary because the thing it helped him approach was already here, fully arrived, indifferent to tools.
findings.Note: Explanatory aphorism riffing on 'tool/indifferent to tools' that over-explains the preceding line instead of trusting it — filler philosophizing.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'Not quite a joke. He meant it exactly.'

findings.Quote: He nodded. Not approval. Understanding - the thing and its mechanism, correctly identified.
findings.Note: Repeats the same 'not X, but Y' hedging pattern used elsewhere in the chapter (ref 1's 'not anger... not respect'), becoming a house tic rather than a fresh observation.
findings.Fix: Vary the construction or cut the appositive clarification.

findings.Quote: for forty of them he had known, the way a man knows something he has decided not to spend, exactly what the Verlaine intake cost
findings.Note: The 'decided not to spend' metaphor doesn't hold up literally — knowledge isn't currency one spends or withholds, and the image muddies rather than clarifies.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'he had known, without ever saying so, exactly what the Verlaine intake cost.'

findings.Quote: not knowing which of them she was choosing when she chose the ink
findings.Note: Abstract wordplay ('choosing... chose the ink') that sounds clever but doesn't clarify what choice is actually being described.
findings.Fix: State plainly what the choice was, e.g., 'not knowing if she'd live to say it in person.'

findings.Quote: the party that had crossed a continent together came apart the way traveling parties do, without ceremony, in a dock square full of other people's business
findings.Note: generic scene-setting aphorism that tells rather than shows the parting's texture
findings.Fix: cut the generalizing clause and let the specific partings carry the weight

findings.Quote: given to her as the one gift a man had left to give
findings.Note: sentimental phrasing that states the emotional significance rather than earning it through image or action
findings.Fix: cut the appositive or replace with something more concrete about what she does with the name

findings.Quote: did not look back
findings.Note: stock exit gesture signaling stoic departure
findings.Fix: specify a concrete physical detail of his walking away instead

findings.Quote: the only kind of loyalty she had left the vocabulary for
findings.Note: abstract, self-consciously literary phrasing that tells the reader how to feel about her loyalty rather than showing it
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete instance of the loyalty in action

findings.Quote: A crater is a wound the world takes and closes.
findings.Note: wound-metaphor opener is a familiar figurative move for describing scarred landscape
findings.Fix: cut the aphoristic frame and open directly on the terraces

findings.Quote: the light that found the bottom was the color of a four-day bruise
findings.Note: strains under literal scrutiny — bruise color-progression is an oddly clinical simile that calls attention to itself rather than landing the image
findings.Fix: replace with a more direct color description or a simpler comparison

findings.Quote: a stillness that meant holding position, and a stillness that meant having seen something, and this was the second kind
findings.Note: overexplained taxonomy of stillness reads as analytical narration rather than observed detail, slightly telling
findings.Fix: cut the categorization and show the specific cue that tips Orim off

findings.Quote: no more force in it than naming a landmark
findings.Note: abstract comparison that doesn't clarify tone or sound of the utterance; reads as reaching for cool detachment rather than depicting it
findings.Fix: describe the actual vocal quality instead of the simile

findings.Quote: which was the intended effect, or was simply what happened, and he did not trouble himself over which
findings.Note: double-hedged construction undercuts the sentence's own claim to precision, feels like authorial waffling rather than character opacity
findings.Fix: cut the hedge or commit to one reading

findings.Quote: the flat unbroken attention of a thing that has looked at one place for the whole of its existence and intends to go on looking
findings.Note: redundant with surrounding text (already established watching for 700 years); over-explains the image
findings.Fix: trim to one clause

findings.Quote: the two facts would sit together in the same hole and decline, politely, to explain each other
findings.Note: personifying abstract 'facts' as polite houseguests is a strained metaphor that doesn't hold up literally
findings.Fix: state plainly that the two truths remain unreconciled

findings.Quote: facts are not defeated, only witnessed and set aside
findings.Note: aphoristic filler-wisdom that generalizes past the scene rather than staying inside it
findings.Fix: cut the maxim, keep the concrete image of the mountain-face

findings.Quote: It had always been here
findings.Note: stock ominous-inevitability phrasing, flattens the otherwise specific cosmic image into genre-standard menace
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific claim tied to the 700-year detail already established

findings.Quote: Eyes of that vintage rarely blink for anyone's convenience.
findings.Note: Quippy aphorism that undercuts the eerie register with cute phrasing.
